findings.passage: line 98: [ -s $D/teacher_ceiling.commit ] && $SAME "$(cat $D/teacher_ceiling.commit)" "$AT" -- eval/teacher_ceiling.py $USES   (SAME="git -c core.fileMode=false diff --quiet", line 37: '# a changed mode alone is not a changed file')
findings.what_is_wrong: core.fileMode only affects how git reads the working tree. The record check compares two commits' trees, where a mode is part of the tree. So a commit whose only change is a mode (chmod +x followed by a commit; the real repo has core.filemode=true) counts as 'another measurement'. The chain then refuses to keep or resume arms whose measurement and imports have identical content. That contradicts the chain's own comment, the stated design ('mode changes alone are ignored'), and the pre-registration's 'kept or resumed only if the measurement and these imports are the same in both'. It fails safe: it stops loudly, measures nothing and releases the lock. But going on then needs either a revert commit or re-measuring the kept arms.
findings.evidence: Sandbox cases b9m and b9mu (cases_b.sh; scratchpad/final_delta/chain/cases_b.out). The first launch crashed at vn, leaving all and allplain complete and 30 rows for vn under C1. Then `chmod +x eval/teacher_ceiling.py` (b9m) or `chmod +x psilm/mlx/model.py` (b9mu) was committed, and git diff --summary showed 'mode change 100644 => 100755'. On relaunch the log shows 'PREREQ all was begun under another measurement (<C1>)', then 'TEMPCONTROL ENDED rc=1', with 0 stub calls and an empty lock dir. `git -c core.fileMode=false diff --raw C1 C2 -- eval/teacher_ceiling.py` prints ':100644 100755 f3a763a f3a763a M' and exits 1: the blob ids are equal and only the mode differs.
findings.proposed:
Compare blob ids, which carry content only, instead of trees. The same function also fixes the next finding. Add after frozen():
```
same_measurement() {   # $1 is a full commit id, and the measurement and its imports hold the same content there as at $AT (modes aside)
  local f
  [ -n "$1" ] && [ "$(git rev-parse -q --verify "$1^{commit}")" = "$1" ] || return 1
  for f in eval/teacher_ceiling.py $USES; do
    [ "$(git rev-parse -q --verify "$1:$f")" = "$(git rev-parse -q --verify "$AT:$f")" ] || return 1
  done
}
```
and on line 98 use `[ -s $D/teacher_ceiling.commit ] && same_measurement "$(cat $D/teacher_ceiling.commit)" \`. I tested this as scratchpad/final_delta/chain/chain_patched.sh on 21 sandbox cases (cases_p.out). In-order run: COMPLETE. Crash then the same commit: vn resumed 30 rows. An unrelated commit, and a commit changing only tempcontrol_reading.py: resumed, COMPLETE. Record absent, empty, garbage, HEAD, short sha, --cached, -R, or a nonexistent 40-hex id: PREREQ. staged.py, bonsai_loader.py or teacher_ceiling.py changed in a commit: PREREQ. Mode-only commits on teacher_ceiling.py or model.py: COMPLETE with vn resumed 30 rows. The lock was released in every case.

findings.what_is_wrong: The record's text is passed to git diff as an argument and never checked to be a commit id. A record that holds an option or a ref therefore passes, and the arm is kept or resumed although the record names no commit. '--cached' makes the call compare the index with AT. '-R' compares AT with the working tree in reverse, which frozen has just made equal. 'HEAD' and 'HEAD~0' resolve to AT. The chain itself always writes the full $AT, so only a hand-edited or corrupted record gets here. For the task's case 'record holds a string that is not a commit', most strings stop the chain correctly, but these do not.
findings.evidence: Sandbox cases b5_* (cases_b.out). vn held 30 rows, relaunched under the same commit. Records 'garbage', ' ', a lone newline, 40 zeros, or a nonexistent 40-hex id each give 'PREREQ vn was begun under another measurement (...)' and ENDED rc=1, with git's 'fatal: bad revision/bad object' in out. Records '--cached', '-R', 'HEAD' and 'HEAD~0' each give 'chain exit 0 ... TEMPCONTROL COMPLETE', and vn's log shows '30 rows resumed'.
findings.proposed: Use the same_measurement() function from the previous finding. Its `[ "$(git rev-parse -q --verify "$1^{commit}")" = "$1" ]` accepts only a full commit id that exists. In the sandbox (cases_p.out: P_b5_HEAD, P_b5___cached, P_b5__R, P_b5_short) every one of these now stops with PREREQ and releases the lock.

findings.passage: 'An arm begun under another commit is kept or resumed only if the measurement and these imports are the same in both.'
findings.what_is_wrong: The text says when an arm is kept, but not what happens otherwise. The chain does not re-measure such an arm. It stops with PREREQ before measuring anything, and the arm's rows and result must be deleted by hand; the record is then overwritten with the new commit. The chain also stops when an arm has rows or a result but its record is absent or empty. It logs this as 'was begun under another measurement ()', which the text does not mention. A reader could take the rule to mean such an arm is measured afresh.
findings.evidence: Sandbox cases b3 (record absent) and b4a (record empty): 'PREREQ vn was begun under another measurement ()', ENDED rc=1, 0 stub calls. Cases b8, b8b and b9 (import or measurement changed in a later commit): PREREQ at the first arm, nothing measured. Case b11 (rows and result deleted by hand): the record is overwritten with the new AT and all nine arms are measured, COMPLETE.
findings.proposed: Append to the_rules_as_applied, and in substance to the header: 'Otherwise, and when an arm has rows or a result but no record of its commit, the chain stops before measuring; the arm is measured again only after its rows and result are removed.' Optionally log 'no record of the commit' instead of '()' when the record is absent or empty.
